title: Loneliness
hookLine: God sets the lonely in families (Psalm 68:6)

cards: Early in Genesis, before anything has gone wrong, before a single bite of fruit, God looks at something and calls it not good. It isn't a sin. It's a man by himself.
"It is not good that the man should be alone." Loneliness is there in the Bible's opening pages, named by God himself as a problem. An apartment where the only voice is the television.
A crowded dorm and nobody to call. A kitchen table set for one after years of setting it for two.

teach.h: GOD SETTETH THE SOLITARY IN FAMILIES.
teach.b: You met that verse in year two; now, what the Bible does with it. Psalm 68 says: "God setteth the solitary in families: he bringeth out those which are bound with chains." Look who stands next to whom.
The solitary, beside the prisoners. The psalm treats loneliness as a kind of captivity, and God as the one who opens the door and walks people into a home. Jesus widens what family means.
In Mark, someone tells him his mother and brothers are outside asking for him.

teach.h: WHOSOEVER DOES THE WILL OF GOD.
teach.b: He looks at the people sitting around him and says: "Behold my mother and my brethren! For whosoever shall do the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and mother."
A family you can be set into, not only born into. Then the cross, in John's Gospel. Jesus is dying, and his mother stands there with the disciple he loved.
He says to her, "Woman, behold thy son!"
And to the disciple, "Behold thy mother!" Then: "And from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home." Even then, he makes sure she won't be left alone.

teach.h: COULD YE NOT WATCH WITH ME?
teach.b: In Gethsemane he asks Peter and two others to stay awake with him, and finds them sleeping: "What, could ye not watch with me one hour?" So loneliness, in these texts, isn't a failure of faith.
Jesus himself asked for company and found his friends asleep. And the setting-in, the psalm's promise, often arrives through a person: someone who calls, who knocks, who takes another person home.

how: Christians care for lonely people through home visits, bringing communion to people who can't leave home, shared meals after services, and small groups; some churches keep lists of members to call or visit regularly.

games.q: you're the disciple standing at the cross. Jesus looks at you and at his mother and says, behold thy mother. what do you do?
o: stay with her until evening, then go home.
take her into your own home from that hour.
leave her to her other relatives.
games.why: and from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home. a family made with one sentence.

practice: Bring to mind someone who might be lonely right now: a neighbor who lost a spouse, a friend who moved away, a coworker who eats lunch alone, a relative nobody calls much anymore.

Let one face come clearly, and if you pray, hold them before God by name. If you're the lonely one and it turns into thoughts of harming yourself, call or text 988 in the US, or reach local emergency help.

wordCard.voice: Loneliness. Being alone when you don't want to be. Genesis calls it not good, and Psalm 68 says God sets the solitary in families.

orig.note: Hebrew: the solitary ones, people on their own — the word in Psalm 68:6 (68:7 in Hebrew Bibles).

carryVoice: Your line: set in families. A week that began with the church doing wrong ends with a door opening. See you tomorrow.
